ei.title: Breaking the Cycle: Solutions to E-waste
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do. If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste. What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world. Right-to-Repair Movement: Empowering Consumers One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair. For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs. The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause. Repairability Index: Information at a Glance In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair. The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead. Repair Cafés: It Takes a Community When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things. The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer. By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future. Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, and she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score. In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.

questions.passage: On her way to a study group meeting, Liz (A)[deliberately / accidentally] dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are (B)[expensive / cheap], and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more (C)[unreasonable / reasonable] option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① accidentally(실수로)+expensive(비싼)+reasonable(합리적인): Liz가 '실수로' 노트북을 떨어뜨렸고, 수리가 '비싼' 경우가 있으며, 새 것을 사는 게 더 '합리적인' 선택처럼 보인다는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ② deliberately(고의로)는 실수로 떨어뜨린 상황과 반대
❌ ③ cheap(값싼)은 '수리가 비싸고 오래 걸린다'는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ unreasonable(불합리한)은 새 것 구입이 '합리적'으로 보인다는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: accidentally=실수로, expensive=비싼, reasonable=합리적인

questions.passage: If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste. What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to (A)[collected / discarded] electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to (B)[toxic / harmless] materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is (C)[decreasing / increasing] at an alarming rate.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① collected(수거된)는 '버려진' 전자 기기를 뜻하는 e-waste 정의와 반대
❌ ② harmless(무해한)는 납 같은 '유독' 물질을 담고 있다는 문맥과 반대
✅ ③ discarded(버려진)+toxic(유독한)+increasing(증가하는): e-waste는 '버려진' 전자 기기를 가리키고, '유독' 물질 때문에 위험하며, 매년 '증가하고' 있다는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ④ decreasing(감소하는)은 매년 경각심을 주는 속도로 '증가한다'는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: discarded=버려진, toxic=유독한, increasing=증가하는

questions.passage: First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to (A)[discard / obtain] the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be (B)[prohibited / encouraged] by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as (C)[difficult / easy] as possible. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① discard(버리다)는 수리에 필요한 부품과 도구를 '얻을' 수 있어야 한다는 문맥과 반대
✅ ② obtain(얻다)+prohibited(금지된)+easy(쉬운): 제3자가 부품을 '얻을' 수 있어야 하고, 소프트웨어 설치를 막는 관행은 법으로 '금지되어야' 하며, 수리를 가능한 한 '쉽게' 만들어야 한다는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ③ encouraged(장려된)는 소비자 제한 관행을 '금지해야' 한다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ difficult(어려운)는 수리를 가능한 한 '쉽게' 만들라는 요구와 반대
det.tip: obtain=얻다, prohibited=금지된, easy=쉬운

det.korean: ③ accidentally → intentionally: 일부 제품은 '의도적으로' 수리하기 어렵게 설계된다
det.analysis:

det.korean: ③ negative → positive: 이 지수는 두 가지 '긍정적인' 효과를 갖도록 설계되었다

det.analysis:

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① benefit(이득): 납 같은 유독 물질을 담은 e-waste가 '이득'이라는 것은 문맥과 반대
✅ ② hazard(위험 요소): 납 같은 유독 물질 때문에 e-waste가 심각한 건강·환경 '위험 요소'라는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ③ resource(자원): 유해성을 강조하는 문맥과 어울리지 않음
❌ ④ tradition(전통): 문맥과 전혀 무관
det.tip: toxic materials such as lead → serious health and environmental hazard(위험 요소)

questions.passage: They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their <u>broken</u> devices.  The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.  The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009.  It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries.  Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world.  Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics.  They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer.  By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 broken과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① damaged: 손상된 (broken과 비슷한 뜻이라 반대가 아님)
❌ ② cheap: 값싼 (의미축이 다름)
✅ ③ intact: 온전한, 손상되지 않은 ← 정답 (broken의 반대)
❌ ④ heavy: 무거운 (관련 없음)
det.tip: broken(고장 난, 부서진) ↔ intact(온전한, 멀쩡한)

questions.passage:
(A) After a long debate, people agreed that every consumer has the <u>right</u> to repair their own devices. This idea became the foundation of a new movement.
(B) When you get to the corner, turn <u>right</u> and walk straight ahead. You will find the small repair shop at the end of the street.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 right의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) has the right to repair는 소비자가 수리할 '권리'를 가진다는 뜻이고, (B) turn right는 모퉁이에서 '오른쪽'으로 돌라는 뜻 ← 정답
❌ ② (A)는 '오른쪽'이 아니라 '권리'
❌ ③ (A)의 right는 '옳은 것'이 아니라 소비자의 '권리'
❌ ④ (B)의 right는 '권리'가 아니라 방향인 '오른쪽'
det.tip: right: (A) 권리(명사) / (B) 오른쪽(방향)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a machine or device used in the home, especially an electrical one, for tasks such as cleaning or cooking"

det.analysis:
❌ ① legislation: 법률, 법 제정 (법안을 만드는 일)
❌ ② manufacturer: 제조업체 (제품을 만드는 회사)
❌ ③ hazard: 위험 요소 (해를 끼칠 수 있는 것)
✅ ④ appliance: 가전제품 (청소·요리 등 집안일에 쓰는, 특히 전기로 작동하는 기기) ← 정답
det.tip: appliance = 집에서 쓰는 전기 기기(가전제품)

questions.passage: Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how __________ (easy) the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: easy(형용사, 쉬운) → easily(부사, 쉽게): 빈칸은 'the product can be repaired(제품이 수리될 수 있다)'라는 동사구를 꾸미는 자리이므로 부사가 와야 한다. '제품이 얼마나 쉽게 수리될 수 있는지'라는 뜻이 되도록 형용사 easy를 부사 easily로 바꾼다.
det.tip: 동사구(can be repaired)를 꾸미는 자리 → 부사 easily

questions.passage: Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are __________ (accomplish), far less e-waste will be generated.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: accomplish(동사, 이루다) → accomplished(과거분사): 빈칸은 'if all these goals are __________'에서 be동사(are) 뒤에 오는 수동태 자리이므로 과거분사가 와야 한다. '이 모든 목표가 달성된다면'이라는 수동의 뜻이 되도록 동사 accomplish를 과거분사 accomplished로 바꾼다.
det.tip: be동사(are) 뒤 수동태 자리 → 과거분사 accomplished

questions.passage: We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to __________ according to the repairability index.  If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.  Repair Cafés: It Takes a Community When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves.  That is why Repair Cafés were started.  They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 label its products(제품에 라벨을 붙이다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① lower its prices(가격을 낮추다): 수리 용이성 지수와 직접 관련 없음
✅ ② label its products(제품에 라벨을 붙이다): 프랑스 시장에서 가전을 팔려는 회사는 수리 용이성 지수에 따라 '제품에 라벨을 붙여야' 한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ③ close its factories(공장을 닫다): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ hire more workers(직원을 더 고용하다): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: according to the repairability index → label its products(지수에 따라 제품에 라벨 부착)

questions.passage: By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and __________.  Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.  Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop?  Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life.  If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 extend their life spans(수명을 늘리다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① increase their prices(가격을 올리다): 기기를 직접 관리하는 문맥과 무관
❌ ② pollute the environment(환경을 오염시키다): e-waste를 줄이려는 긍정 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ waste more energy(에너지를 더 낭비하다): 지속 가능성을 추구하는 문맥과 반대
✅ ④ extend their life spans(수명을 늘리다): 사람들이 기기를 직접 관리하고 '수명을 늘릴' 수 있게 한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
det.tip: maintain their devices and extend their life spans(기기를 관리하고 수명을 늘리다)
